# v1.5.0 — Languages and invitation review

This release adds Dutch, German, and Spanish, a new way to invite people with a
review step before anything is sent, and per-event control over what guests see
of the RSVP lists. It also enforces a nonce-based script Content Security Policy.
It adds two database migrations that only add columns, and no required
environment variables. Existing event links, RSVP edit links, and sign-ins are
preserved.

## Changes

### New features

- Choose Dutch, German, or Spanish from the language button in the header (a 文A
  icon with the current language code). The choice is saved to your account
  and browser, and system emails and text messages use each recipient's saved
  language. Unknown recipients still receive English. The menu lists English
  first, then the other languages alphabetically. (#732, #747, #748, #751, #763,
  #764, #765)
- Invite people by typing names and contacts, pasting a list, or importing a CSV
  or spreadsheet, up to 200 at a time. Before sending, review recipients grouped
  as ready, already invited, already responded, or can't send, and preview each
  invitation. (#752, #755)
- Control guest-facing RSVP display per event: show, collapse, or hide each
  response list, and show exact, capped, or no counts. (#668, #669)
- Invitation emails keep the invitee's personal link in the event details. (#713)

### Security

- Enforce a nonce-based script Content Security Policy and block injected
  inline scripts and base-URL retargeting. (#695)
- Remediate dependency audit findings, and ship only production dependencies in
  the container image. (#688, #694, #707, #741, #742)

### Fixes

- Resend from the guest list now goes through the reviewed invitation flow. It
  refuses stale or already-answered invitations and explains how to send one
  deliberately. (#758, #762)
- Fix the edit-link warning shown to invited guests. (#755)

### Maintenance

- Update Next.js to 16.4.2, React to 19.3.1, iron-session to 9.0.1, Nodemailer
  to 10.1.7, Prisma to 7.10.1, Sharp to 0.35.5, and Zod to 4.6.7, and add
  next-intl 4.14.9.
- Bundle the Roboto theme font locally to avoid an upstream build failure.
- Update the optional email worker's Wrangler toolchain. The worker API is
  unchanged; this release does not deploy the worker.
- Refresh the README with application screenshots. (#666)

## Upgrade from v1.4.1

1. Back up the database, uploads, and `.env`; record the running image digest.
2. If a reverse proxy or CDN sits in front of the app, make sure it does not
   cache or replay page HTML. Each page now carries a per-request script nonce,
   so a cached page would block its own scripts. Static files under `/_next/`
   and `public/` can still be cached.
3. In your deployment Compose file, pin the app image to
   `ghcr.io/joe-cole1/rsvp-to-me:1.5.0` after the Release workflow has published it.
   Container tags omit the Git release tag's leading `v`.
4. With the standard production configuration, run:

   ```bash
   docker compose -f docker-compose.release.yml pull app
   docker compose -f docker-compose.release.yml up -d --no-deps app
   docker compose -f docker-compose.release.yml logs --tail=100 app
   ```

5. Startup applies two migrations: `20260927044500_guest_rsvp_display` adds six
   event display settings, and `20261019000000_user_preferred_locale` adds an
   optional language preference to each user. Existing events keep expanded
   lists and exact counts. Events created afterwards default to a collapsed
   "Can't make it" list with no guest-facing count.
6. Check health, sign-in, language switching, event creation, public and
   protected RSVPs, RSVP editing, uploads, inviting people through the review
   step, and delivery through the email/SMS providers enabled on your site.

Run these commands in the existing deployment directory with its existing
project name, mounts, and secrets. If you use a custom Compose file, retain that
configuration and update only the app image. This upgrade does not require
upgrading PostgreSQL or Redis.

Existing sign-ins stay valid: iron-session 9 reads cookies written by version 8.
For Docker installations, Node 22 is included in the image. Source installations
must use the repository's supported Node 22/npm 10 versions and reinstall from
the lockfiles.

## Rollback and known limitations

For a rollback to v1.4.1, pin the app to the previously recorded image digest
(or `ghcr.io/joe-cole1/rsvp-to-me:1.4.1`) and recreate only the app container.
No database restore is needed. The new columns are nullable or have defaults, so
v1.4.1 keeps working with them, and its startup finds no pending migrations.
While rolled back, saved language preferences and display settings are ignored
and the UI is English. Both come back if you upgrade again. Restoring an older
backup would discard newer RSVPs.

Builds still download the remaining Google fonts through Next.js and can
encounter the tracked upstream font-query failure. Fonts are served locally at
runtime. Provider tests use mocks; passing CI does not confirm delivery through
your live email or SMS account. Translated pages fall back to English wherever
a translation is missing.

See the [upgrade guide](https://github.com/joe-cole1/rsvp-to-me/blob/main/docs/admin/upgrading.md)
for backup, verification, and release approval procedures.

**Full comparison:** https://github.com/joe-cole1/rsvp-to-me/compare/v1.4.1...v1.5.0
